thread:
alex: Heads-up — after last night's kernel 6.1.12 rollout in eu-west we started seeing a subset of inference nodes (~40) hit persistent NCCL hangs during long multi-GPU jobs. Symptoms: jobs stall on all-reduce, driver logs show `UNEXPECTED_SYMBOL` when loading `nvidia.ko`. Suspect kernel-module ABI mismatch with the pinned driver package.

maria: Ack. Do we know which driver version is on those hosts vs what the package server pushed? :eyes:

alex: Quick scan shows nodes are running nvidia-driver-535 from our image, but the kernel packages were updated to 6.1.12 from 6.1.9 — some kernels were produced with different module layout. Looks like module build didn't happen for the new kernel variant, so the installed .ko is incompatible.

jim: Rough plan: 1) pin driver package on affected pools, 2) rebuild nvidia module for 6.1.12 via DKMS and promote, 3) if rebuild fails, rollback kernel for those hosts. Keep canary small. Who can own step 2?

nina: I can kick off DKMS rebuilds against the 6.1.12 kernel image in staging. If that passes, we can surface a compat shim artifact and roll it via the image-builder. If rebuild fails under some configs, fallback = kernel rollback as jim said.

alex: Good. Immediate hotfix actions I propose now: a) place apt/yum hold on driver package to stop further changes for the next 24h, b) mark eu-west compute pool as "driver-compat-hold" in our fleet control plane, c) start DKMS rebuild canary on 5 nodes.

maria: For apt (debian images) the hold commands:

```
# freeze the driver package
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535
# if we need to install a specific stable build
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-535=535.54-0ubuntu1
```

For RHEL-based images (rpm):

```
# pin with dnf
sudo dnf versionlock add nvidia-driver-535-535.54
```

jim: Also add a host-level kernel-module sanity check in the init script to fail fast and let autoscaler replace the node before a long job is scheduled. Sample check:

```
if ! modinfo nvidia >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "nvidia module missing or incompatible" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

nina: Canary status: started DKMS rebuild on staging-5 at 1818005567. First build succeeded, nvidia.ko loaded and all-reduce passes a small NCCL smoke test. I'll queue 4 more canaries across different hw configs.

alex: Nice. Ops action items for rollout manager:
- put eu-west and eu-west-burst pools on holdlist (no new kernel upgrades)
- pin driver packages across pools (script below)
- start 5-node DKMS canary ramp -> full rebuild promotion if green
- if any canary fails, trigger kernel rollback playbook

ops-bot: holdlist updated: eu-west, eu-west-burst added by alex at 1818005582 :white_check_mark:

maria: Quick RP for the pin script (debian/ubuntu):

```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
nodes="$@"
for n in $nodes; do
  ssh $n "sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535 || true"
  ssh $n "sudo systemctl restart image-update || true"
done
```

alex: Cost/availability note: holding drivers blocks kernel upgrades which may delay some security patches. We should target a narrow hold window (24–48h) and document compensating controls (network-level WAF, host firewall rules applied via config management).

jim: If DKMS route is successful we should also publish a kernel-module compatibility matrix in the infra-runbook and add an automated test to our CI that runs module builds against new kernel images before promotion.

nina: Agreed. I'll draft the matrix: kernel versions on rows, driver minor versions as columns, results = build/pass/fail. Will post link when ready.

alex: OK actionable summary:
1) maria apply package holds (in progress) 1818005589
2) nina run DKMS canary and report (in progress)
3) jim add init-module sanity check to image (todo)
4) ops-bot set holdlist and block kernel promotion (done)

Please react with :thumbsup: when you have completed your step.

maria: applied holds to the remaining 38 nodes in the pool at 1818005596 :thumbsup:

nina: canaries all green on 5 nodes, starting batch rebuild (30 nodes) at 1818005599 :white_check_mark:

jim: PR opened for init check: https://git.redwood.dev/infra/ami-images/pull/324 (small snippet, tests included)

alex: If the 30-node batch is green we'll promote the compat shim artifact and schedule a controlled driver rebuild job overnight. If anything regresses we revert kernel in the affected hosts and unblock with a postmortem. Thanks team — keep updates in this thread.
